key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV degradation in perovskite devices, identifying preferential damage at the buried hole-transport-layer interface.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables rapid screening of buried-interface treatments to improve the UV stability of perovskite solar cells.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different depths with photoluminescence.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL, and ideality-factor measurements during UV-soaking studies.
Compare perovskite films and devices with different indium tin oxide surface modifiers.
evidence_signal: Nondestructive measurements localized UV damage consistently with ex-situ destructive tests and showed reduced damage and improved UV stability with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification.
watch_item: Depth sensitivity depends on wavelength-dependent absorption; the abstract does not establish quantitative depth resolution or generality beyond the tested UV-soaking conditions.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
